concerns.text: The plan proposes stratifying the 80/20 split by 'Chemical Family' to control for compositional bias. However, the spec (FR-004a) and data model do not define 'Chemical Family' as a derived feature or provide a mapping logic. If this stratification variable is not explicitly engineered and available in the dataset, the split will default to random or fail, invalidating the claim of controlling for compositional bias. The plan must specify the exact algorithm or source for deriving 'Chemical Family' from the formula.

The plan states: 'If VIF > 10, log warning but do NOT remove features.' While this handles multicollinearity for prediction, the research question asks to 'evaluate the correlation' and 'rank' descriptors. In the presence of high multicollinearity (VIF > 10), tree-based feature importance (Gini/impurity) and even permutation importance become unstable and biased toward one of the correlated features arbitrarily. The plan lacks a method to disentangle these effects (e.g., conditional permutation importance, SHAP interaction values, or orthogonalization) before ranking, meaning the resulting 'ranking' may not reflect true causal or predictive contribution of individual descriptors.

The plan mentions 'Power Analysis: With 12.5k samples, power is sufficient...'. This is a post-hoc assertion without a defined effect size or statistical test for the power calculation. To validate the claim that the sample size is sufficient to detect the intended effect (correlation between descriptors and formation energy), the plan must specify the minimum detectable effect size (e.g., Cohen's f²) and the alpha level used for this power analysis, or defer this to the research phase as a `[deferred]` value rather than asserting sufficiency.

concerns.location: plan.md:Constitution Check -> VII. Statistical Evaluation Rigor
concerns.text: The plan claims to implement 'paired t-tests for performance comparison' (referencing Constitution Principle VII) but the methodology section only lists R², MAE, RMSE, and permutation importance. There is no explicit plan for how the paired t-test will be conducted (e.g., comparing RF vs GB on the same folds) or how the p-values will be adjusted for multiple comparisons if multiple metrics are tested. Without this, the 'Statistical Evaluation Rigor' claim is unsupported by the proposed analysis steps.
